misconceptions.description: The largest or best-known town is the capital (Ganta for Nimba).
misconceptions.feedback: Ganta is Nimba's biggest trading town, but the county is administered from Sanniquellie.

misconceptions.description: Monrovia is the capital of Montserrado as well as of Liberia, or the national capital is also every county's capital.
misconceptions.probe: Two-part item: national capital, then Montserrado's county seat
misconceptions.feedback: Liberia's capital and Montserrado's county seat are different roles.

misconceptions.description: Counties that are next to each other in a list are next to each other on the map (Maryland and Sinoe).
misconceptions.feedback: Look at the map: Grand Kru lies between them.

misconceptions.description: Confusing the four 'Grand' counties (Bassa, Cape Mount, Gedeh, Kru) and their capitals.
misconceptions.feedback: A position cue: Cape Mount far west, Bassa central coast, Kru south-east coast, Gedeh east interior.

misconceptions.description: The capital governs the county, or the county elects its own government.
misconceptions.probe: Constructed item ft01-a2 and a true/false item
misconceptions.feedback: The capital is where the county administration sits. The superintendent is appointed by the President.

mediaSpecifications.requirement: An accessible county map (SVG): each county labelled on focus, keyboard-navigable, with a text table grouping counties as coastal and interior, west to east.
mediaSpecifications.offlineFallback: A printable A4 outline map and a two-column county/capital table.

mediaSpecifications.requirement: Place-the-capital interaction: drag or select the capital into its county, with immediate, misconception-specific feedback (e.g. choosing Ganta for Nimba).
mediaSpecifications.offlineFallback: Paper cut-out capital cards placed on the printed map; a teacher answer sheet.

mediaSpecifications.requirement: A 'capital versus largest town' contrast card for Nimba and Montserrado.
mediaSpecifications.offlineFallback: The same card as a text box in the printable pack.

items: Five county–capital pairs drawn at random, always including Nimba and one of the five counties the legacy lesson omitted
Locate two counties on a blank map

assessmentTasks.task: Blank map: write the capital of each of the 15 counties (key: the reviewer-confirmed list).
A classmate writes 'Ganta is the capital of Nimba because it is the biggest town.' Explain the error and correct it.
Four items whose distractors are mapped to M1–M4.
On the lesson's county map, name the counties a traveller crosses going by the coast from Buchanan to Greenville, and justify the order from the map.

misconceptions.description: The bubbles in boiling water are air.
misconceptions.feedback: The large bubbles in boiling water are water vapour forming inside the liquid. The first tiny bubbles when you start heating are dissolved air coming out.

misconceptions.description: The temperature keeps rising while ice melts, or a mixture can get hotter than its hottest part.
misconceptions.feedback: While ice is melting, the energy goes into changing state and the temperature stays near 0 °C.

misconceptions.description: Water on a cold bottle leaks through the plastic.
misconceptions.feedback: Water vapour from the air condenses on the cold surface.
Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature; boiling happens throughout the liquid at the boiling point.

misconceptions.description: The particles themselves expand or melt.
misconceptions.feedback: The particles stay the same; their spacing and motion change.
No new substance forms, and the change reverses.

mediaSpecifications.requirement: A particle simulation with a heat slider showing arrangement and motion in each state, with a text description of every state.
mediaSpecifications.offlineFallback: A printed three-panel particle diagram and a role-play (learners as particles).

mediaSpecifications.requirement: A heating curve for water with labelled plateaus, built step by step.
mediaSpecifications.offlineFallback: A printed graph with a data table.

mediaSpecifications.requirement: An optional low-cost demonstration: ice in a cup with a thermometer, read every minute (teacher-led; safety note).
mediaSpecifications.offlineFallback: A recorded data table for classes without ice or a thermometer.

items: Name the change of state in three scenes
What happens to the temperature while ice melts

assessmentTasks.task: Draw particles of palm oil as a liquid and as a solid, and label the differences.
Explain why wet clothes dry on a line without boiling.
Data: a drink with ice reads 0 °C for 8 minutes, then rises. Explain the pattern using particles and energy.
Five items whose distractors are mapped to M1–M6.

misconceptions.description: Add the numerators and the denominators (1/4 + 1/2 = 2/6).
misconceptions.feedback: The size of the parts doesn't change when you combine them. Make the parts the same size first.

misconceptions.description: A bigger denominator means a bigger fraction.
misconceptions.feedback: More parts in the same whole means each part is smaller.
5/4 is one whole and one more quarter.

misconceptions.description: Losing track of the whole (a fraction of a bag versus kilograms).
misconceptions.feedback: Say what the whole is before writing the fraction.

misconceptions.description: Unequal parts can be named as fractions.

mediaSpecifications.requirement: A fraction-bar and number-line manipulative: split, shade and place fractions, and see equivalence by splitting.
mediaSpecifications.offlineFallback: Paper strips folded into halves, quarters and eighths.

mediaSpecifications.requirement: A comparison tool: drag two fractions onto one number line.
mediaSpecifications.offlineFallback: A printed number line from 0 to 2.

assessmentTasks.task: Place four fractions (including 1 and 5/4) on a number line.
Four sums and differences, two with related denominators.
Which is more rice: 2/3 of a cup or 3/5 of a cup? Justify in two ways.
